# Pipeline Runbook {#sec-runbook}

## Read First

This runbook takes a fresh Ubuntu server to crossing-distance measurements from two imagery sources, segmented by one model, on a stratified sample of Cook County intersections. Modal does all GPU and bulk-fetch work. The scripts are in `crosswalk_pipeline.tar.gz` and unpack into `~/crosswalk/pipeline`.

The design behind these steps — the two imagery candidates (A, Google Maps; B, Cook County 3-band RGB), why SAM 3 replaces the reference methodology's SAM 2.1, the SAM 3 configuration options, the benchmark and fine-tuning results, and the sample design — is in [Crossing Distance: Imagery Source and Segmentation Model Comparison](phase01_crosswalk_models.html). This appendix covers only how to run it. The R equivalents of steps 4.2–4.4 are in [Appendix A: Data Preparation Code](dataprep.html).

::: {.callout-note}
## What has and hasn't been tested

Run on Modal so far: zero-shot benchmark rounds (`zs2`, `zs3`), fine-tuning run `ft1`, and holdout runs `ho_zs`, `ho_ft1`, `ho_ft1_last`; results are in `data/modeling/`.

Tested locally on 2026-10-08:

- Segmentation helpers on a synthetic clip georeferenced exactly as the fetcher writes it: pixel area within 0.3%, polygon area within 0.2%.
- The reference grow-cut, unchanged, measured a 12 m crossing at 39.51 ft (true 39.37 ft).
- Exemplar boxes land 15 m out on every approach leg and lie wholly on a 12 m road.
- Boundary F1 at 0.5 m separates a 0.3 m curb error (1.00) from a 1 m error (0.50), while IoU barely moves (0.98).
- The fusion and negative-class decision rules.
- Benchmark preparation on a synthetic COCO export with Roboflow-style file names.
- Sample selection on the project's 169,456-point intersection layer.
- Fine-tuning plumbing on a randomly initialised SAM 3 (CPU): gradients reach only the segmentation head, and the saved head reloads. Also the curb weighting, the augmentation and the holdout split, which has no original shared across holdout, validation and training.

Not yet run: the county pilot check (4.8), the evaluation-sample fetch and segmentation (4.9–4.10), and grow-cut on SAM 3 output (4.11). Expect small fixes on the first run.
:::

| Script | Runs on | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `00_osm_crossings.py` | server | Reference `osm_ingest_local` for Cook County → OSM crossing edges |
| `01_build_candidates.py` | server | Intersections with an OSM crossing ≤ 25 m, tagged Chicago/suburban + Google tile position |
| `cc_fetch.py` | Modal CPU | 50 m clips: Google z22 (A), county RGB (B), county RGB+NIR (canopy pool) |
| `02_select_sample.py` | server | Stratified evaluation sample + separate pilot set |
| `02b_osm_roads.py` | server | Optional: OSM drivable centre-lines around clips, for box prompts (also done locally in [Appendix A](dataprep.html)) |
| `cc_weights.py` | Modal | SAM 3 checkpoint from Hugging Face to a volume; GPU smoke test |
| `04_bench_prep.py` | server | Public curb dataset → images, ground-truth road masks, OSM prompt boxes |
| `cc_benchmark.py` | Modal GPU | Scores every SAM 3 configuration against the labels (IoU, boundary F1); `--subset holdout`, `--delta` |
| `05_make_holdout.py` | server | Holdout / validation / training split of the curb dataset by original image |
| `cc_finetune.py` | Modal GPU | Fine-tunes SAM 3's segmentation head on the curb labels → `seg_head_best.pt`, `seg_head_last.pt` |
| `cc_segment.py` | Modal GPU | Chosen configuration → `cross_walks.geojson` + QA overlays; pilot grid mode |
| `03_grow_cut.sh` | server | Reference grow-cut, unchanged → `refined_crosswalks_v3_0_4.csv` (`length_ft`) |
| `cc_sam3.py`, `cc_geom.py`, `cc_common.py` | shared | SAM 3 core; box geometry and metrics; constants |

: Pipeline scripts {.striped}

## Server Sizing

Recommended: **8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, 250 GB SSD, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, no GPU.** The server is an orchestrator; SAM 3 inference and bulk fetches run on Modal.

| Resource | Minimum | Recommended | What drives it |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPU | 4 vCPU | 8 vCPU | OSM graph build for all of Cook County (long, mostly single-threaded); grow-cut; R/Quarto alongside |
| RAM | 16 GB | 32 GB | `osm_ingest_local` loads the full, unsimplified `network_type="all"` graph for the county — the largest single job |
| Disk | 100 GB | 250 GB SSD | OS + environments ~25 GB; OSM cache + outputs < 5 GB; QA images and benchmark < 2 GB |
| GPU | none | none | Runs on Modal (L4 for the smoke test, L40S for benchmark and segmentation) |
| OS | Ubuntu 22.04 | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS | uv supplies Python regardless of system Python |

: Server resources {.striped}

Add 8 GB of swap so an OSM build that overshoots RAM slows down instead of being killed:

```bash
sudo fallocate -l 8G /swapfile && sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile && sudo swapon /swapfile
```

## 1. Ubuntu Server Setup

The server gets two Python environments: one for the Modal pipeline, and one for the reference repo, which supplies OSM crossing extraction and grow-cut and runs locally only.

1. System packages:

    ```bash
    sudo apt update && sudo apt -y upgrade
    sudo apt -y install git curl build-essential tmux unzip \
        gdal-bin libgdal-dev libspatialindex-dev osmium-tool
    ```

2. Install uv:

    ```bash
    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
    source ~/.bashrc
    ```

3. Unpack the scripts and add working folders:

    ```bash
    cd ~ && tar xzf crosswalk_pipeline.tar.gz     # files land in ~/crosswalk/pipeline
    mkdir -p ~/crosswalk/data/{inputs,osm,sample,results,bench} ~/crosswalk/logs
    ```

4. Pipeline environment (Modal 1.x, geopandas, osmnx, roboflow):

    ```bash
    cd ~/crosswalk/pipeline
    uv python install 3.12
    uv sync
    uv run python -c "import modal, geopandas, osmnx, roboflow; print(modal.__version__)"
    ```

5. Reference repo, cloned inside the pipeline folder (the scripts expect this path):

    ```bash
    cd ~/crosswalk/pipeline
    git clone https://github.com/agupta01/crossing-distances.git
    cd crossing-distances
    uv sync                        # uses its uv.lock: Python 3.12, pandas 2.3, modal 0.77
    uv pip install osmnx semver    # osmnx is imported but missing from its pyproject
    ```

    Keep grow-cut in this locked environment: under pandas 3.x it fails with `TypeError: Invalid value '[]' for dtype 'int64'`.

6. Copy the project's intersections into the inputs folder:

    ```bash
    cp <path-to>/crosswalk-distances-cc/output/all_intersections.* ~/crosswalk/data/inputs/
    ```

Run long jobs inside `tmux new -s cw` so they survive a dropped SSH session.

## 2. Modal Setup

All project objects live in one Modal environment, `cook`.

1. Create an account at [modal.com](https://modal.com) and add billing ([pricing](https://modal.com/pricing)).

2. Authenticate the server. In the Modal dashboard, go to Settings → API Tokens → **New token**. The secret is shown only once, so copy the full `modal token set …` command and run it on the server prefixed with `uv run`. Alternatively, `uv run modal token new` prints a URL to approve in any logged-in browser.

3. Create and select the environment:

    ```bash
    cd ~/crosswalk/pipeline
    uv run modal environment create cook
    uv run modal config set-environment cook
    echo 'export MODAL_ENVIRONMENT=cook' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc
    ```

4. Create the volumes:

    ```bash
    for v in cc-imagery cc-sam3-weights cc-results; do uv run modal volume create $v; done
    ```

    | Volume | Holds |
    |---|---|
    | `cc-imagery` | `/A_google`, `/B_cook_rgb`, `/pool_rgbn`, `/pilot_A`, `/pilot_B` GeoTIFF clips |
    | `cc-sam3-weights` | `/sam3/sam3.pt`, `/sam3/config.json` |
    | `cc-results` | `/inputs/osm_roads.geojson`; `/bench` (benchmark data); `/bench_runs/<run>`; `/<folder>/<run>/` segmentation outputs |

5. Verify with a one-clip fetch. Create `~/crosswalk/data/sample/test.csv` containing `id,lat,lon` and `x,41.878123,-87.629456` on two lines, then:

    ```bash
    uv run modal run cc_fetch.py --source B --input ../data/sample/test.csv --out-csv ../logs/test_B.csv
    uv run modal volume ls --env cook cc-imagery /B_cook_rgb
    ```

    Expect `done: 1 ok, 0 failed`. Files live on the Modal volume, not the server; `/imagery/...` paths in logs are container paths. Use `modal volume get` to download any file for inspection. The local destination must be a folder that already exists; a remote folder is written inside it under its own name (e.g. `/bench_runs/zs1` → `…/bench/zs1/`).

## 3. SAM 3 and Data Access

SAM 3 runs inside a Modal container image defined in `cc_segment.py` (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.10 for CUDA 12.8, SAM 3 from Meta's GitHub). Nothing is installed on the server.

::: {.callout-tip}
## SAM 3 vs. SAM 3.1
SAM 3.1's change (Object Multiplex) applies to video tracking only, so still images use the SAM 3 image checkpoint (`facebook/sam3`, `sam3.pt`). See [the model section of the comparison chapter](phase01_crosswalk_models.html).
:::

1. **SAM 3 weights.** Request access at [huggingface.co/facebook/sam3](https://huggingface.co/facebook/sam3) (accept Meta's licence terms; wait for approval). Create a read token under Settings → Access Tokens, store it as a Modal secret, then download and smoke-test:

    ```bash
    uv run modal secret create huggingface HF_TOKEN=hf_XXXX
    uv run modal run cc_weights.py --action download
    uv run modal run cc_weights.py --action smoke-test
    ```

    The first run builds the SAM 3 image (several minutes, once). Expect `OK: torch 2.10…, GPU NVIDIA L4, prompt 'road' -> N instance(s)`.

2. **Roboflow API key** (for the benchmark dataset). Create a free account at [roboflow.com](https://roboflow.com) and copy your API key from workspace settings. Use the project's own key; the reference repo's notebook contains the original authors' key, which should not be used.

    ```bash
    echo 'export ROBOFLOW_API_KEY=xxxx' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc
    ```

## 4. Run the Comparison Pipeline

Run every command from `~/crosswalk/pipeline` with `MODAL_ENVIRONMENT=cook` exported unless a step says otherwise. Each step ends with its check.

### 4.1 OSM crossing edges for Cook County

Server, 30–90 min, the RAM-heavy step. Uses the reference repo's own extraction, so the lines grow-cut measures along match the reference method:

```bash
cd ~/crosswalk/pipeline/crossing-distances
nohup uv run python ../00_osm_crossings.py --place "Cook County, Illinois, USA" \
    --out ~/crosswalk/data/osm > ~/crosswalk/logs/osm_ingest.log 2>&1 &
tail -f ~/crosswalk/logs/osm_ingest.log
```

If Overpass times out, add `--overpass-url https://overpass.kumi.systems/api`. **Check:** `data/osm/crosswalk_edges_v2_0.shp` exists and holds tens of thousands of lines.

### 4.2 Candidate pool

```bash
cd ~/crosswalk/pipeline
uv run python 01_build_candidates.py --intersections ../data/inputs/all_intersections.shp \
    --crosswalk-edges ../data/osm/crosswalk_edges_v2_0.shp \
    --out ../data/sample/candidates.csv --pool-per-group 300
```

Keeps intersections with an OSM crossing within 25 m (measured in EPSG:3435), labels them `chicago`/`suburban`, computes `tile_offset` (0 = centre, 1 = edge of the zoom-19 Web Mercator tile), and draws up to 300 per geography. **Check:** the printed count per group is 300.

### 4.3 Canopy screen

```bash
uv run modal run cc_fetch.py --source pool --input ../data/sample/candidates.csv \
    --out-csv ../data/sample/pool_ndvi.csv
```

Each 4-band clip gets `veg_frac`, the share of pixels with NDVI > 0.2. **Check:** `veg_frac` spreads between 0 and ~0.8, with few `error` rows.

### 4.4 Evaluation sample and pilot set

```bash
uv run python 02_select_sample.py --candidates ../data/sample/candidates.csv \
    --ndvi ../data/sample/pool_ndvi.csv --n 150 --n-pilot 30 \
    --out ../data/sample/sample.csv --pilot-out ../data/sample/pilot.csv
```

The evaluation sample has 8 strata (geography × canopy high/low terciles × tile centre/edge) of 19 each, 152 in total; the pilot set is 30 other intersections. **Check:** the printed stratum table; thin cells mean the pool needs to be larger (`--pool-per-group 600` in 4.2).

### 4.5 OSM road centre-lines for box prompts (optional)

**Optional: run only if a configuration with box prompts (`box` or `text+box`) is adopted.** `cc_segment.py` reads this file only for those modes. The leading configuration (fine-tuned head, text prompt "road") never uses it. Box prompts are not supported by the evidence so far: on the 6 benchmark clips that could take boxes, the best `text+box` setting scored boundary F1 0.25, against 0.34 for text alone, and box-only 0.20 (`zs2`). Six clips is too few to rule boxes out; a fair test needs an unaugmented fork of the benchmark dataset (see 4.6).

The same file can be built locally from the Cook County OSM extract, without Overpass, in [Appendix A: Data Preparation Code](dataprep.html) (chunk `osm-box-roads`); then only the `modal volume put` line below is needed. On the server:

```bash
uv run python 02b_osm_roads.py --inputs ../data/sample/sample.csv,../data/sample/pilot.csv \
    --out ../data/sample/osm_roads.geojson
uv run modal volume put --env cook cc-results ../data/sample/osm_roads.geojson /inputs/osm_roads.geojson
```

Drivable classes only (trunk, primary, secondary, tertiary, unclassified, residential, living streets, busways, and motorway links); service roads, alleys, and private access are excluded. **Check:** a few thousand lines; open the file in QGIS over the sample points.

### 4.6 Benchmark on labelled data

Choose the SAM 3 configuration by measurement, not by eye. The public [Satellite Curb Segmentation](https://universe.roboflow.com/pcd-rxiqe/satellite-curb-segmentation) dataset (CC BY 4.0) is hand-labelled Google clips of US intersections from the reference study, with sidewalks, buildings, parks, and refuge islands marked non-drivable — exactly this task.

```bash
uv run python 04_bench_prep.py --list-versions          # pick the version with the reference clips
uv run python 04_bench_prep.py --version 15 --out ../data/bench
uv run modal volume rm --env cook -r cc-results /bench      # clear any earlier benchmark set (ignore 'not found')
uv run modal volume put --env cook cc-results ../data/bench /bench
uv run modal run cc_benchmark.py --run-name zs1
mkdir -p ../data/results/bench
uv run modal volume get --env cook --force cc-results /bench_runs/zs1 ../data/results/bench/
```

`04_bench_prep.py` uses all splits and drops Roboflow's augmented duplicates (copies named `<original>.rf.<hash>.jpg`), keeping the test/valid copy where one exists. It prints a table of image sources: version 6 mixes the reference study's coordinate-named Google clips with Esri patches (e.g. `boston_patch_2_esri`) and screenshots. OSM boxes can only be placed on unaugmented clips whose file names carry coordinates; all other images are scored with text prompts, and box-mode configurations fall back to text on them (`box_fallback` in the summary). Choose the version first: `--list-versions` prints each version's image count, splits, date, and augmentation. Version 6 — the one named in the reference repo's notebook — now holds only 15 Esri patches and screenshots and no coordinate-named clips, so it cannot benchmark box prompts or stand in for Google imagery. Version 15 (May 2025) is the reference study's set: 579 training images are 193 originals × 3 augmented copies, plus 15 test images. After de-duplication it yields 208 images, 165 of them coordinate-named Google clips (157 train, 8 test); the rest are Esri patches, screenshots, and clips named by ID. Text-prompt configurations are scored on all 208. OSM boxes go only on the 8 unaugmented test clips, too few to judge box modes. To evaluate box prompts on all 165 clips, fork the dataset into your own Roboflow workspace (Fork Dataset on its Universe page), generate a version with no augmentation, and run the prep with `--workspace <your-workspace> --project <your-project> --version <N>`. The default grid is 45 configurations: 3 modes × 3 fusions × 4 phrases ("road", "street", "roadway", "asphalt road") × with/without negatives. Box-only mode has no phrase, and instance fusion has no negatives, which brings the count down from the full product to 45.

In `../data/results/bench/zs1/`, `summary.csv` ranks configurations by mean **boundary F1 at 0.5 m** — how closely the predicted road edge follows the true curb, the quantity grow-cut cuts on — with IoU alongside. `summary_by_source.csv` repeats the scores by image source and by whether OSM boxes were available; judge box modes only on the `has_boxes = True` rows, and give most weight to the coordinate-named Google clips, which match candidate A's imagery. The 0.5 m tolerance assumes a 50 m clip; for Esri patches and screenshots the scale is unknown, so there it is a fixed ~10 px tolerance, comparable across configurations but not in metres. Review `qa/<config>/` for the top few: road tinted, predicted edge magenta, true curb green, prompt boxes yellow.

**Round 2 (after the first run).** If the best first-round setting under-calls road (`area_ratio_median` well below 1, because parked cars, crosswalk paint and shadows are left out and each hole adds a false edge), run a second grid that tests fixes for it:

```bash
uv run modal run cc_benchmark.py --run-name zs3 --modes text --fusions fused \
    --prompt-sets "road;road,car,crosswalk" --negative-sets ";sidewalk,grass,building,tree" \
    --prob-thds 0.3,0.2,0.15 --fill-holes 0,10,25 --rules positive,complement
```

45 configurations. `summary.csv` now also reports boundary F1 at 1.0 m (`bf1_1m_mean`) and the median predicted/true road area (`area_ratio_median`, below 1 = road under-called).

Record the best zero-shot setting and its scores as the baseline in `data/results/README` (the current results are summarized in the comparison chapter). If its boundary F1 is too weak to hand to grow-cut, fine-tune (4.7) and compare on held-out clips before choosing.

### 4.7 Fine-tune SAM 3 on the curb labels

Zero-shot SAM 3's notion of "road" is not the labels' notion of drivable surface (curb to curb, parked cars and paint included). `cc_finetune.py` retrains only SAM 3's segmentation head — 2.3 M of its ~850 M parameters: the pixel decoder, the prompt cross-attention and the semantic head — on the curb dataset, with the image and text encoders frozen. The loss is binary cross-entropy weighted up to 5× within about 1 m of a true curb, plus Dice. Training adds random rotations, flips and mild colour jitter on top of Roboflow's own augmented copies. The result is a small file (about 10 MB) that is loaded on top of the standard SAM 3 checkpoint, so one model serves both candidates.

**Split by original image.** Roboflow stores three augmented copies of each training image, so the split is made by original name: a copy of a test image in training would leak its labels. `05_make_holdout.py` sets aside 40 coordinate-named Google clips as the **holdout** (all 8 test-split clips, then 32 random training originals; seed 2026) and 15 other originals as **validation**, used only to pick the best epoch. Everything else is training data (about 450 images with copies).

```bash
# training set: all splits, augmented copies kept, no OSM boxes
uv run python 04_bench_prep.py --version 15 --keep-duplicates --no-osm --out ../data/train_full
uv run modal volume put --env cook --force cc-results ../data/train_full /train_full

# holdout / validation / training split, from the de-duplicated benchmark set of 4.6
uv run python 05_make_holdout.py --meta ../data/bench/meta.json --out ../data/bench/holdout.json
uv run modal volume put --env cook --force cc-results ../data/bench/holdout.json /bench/holdout.json

# plumbing test (~5 min): 20 images, one validation pass before and after
uv run modal run cc_finetune.py --run-name smoke --epochs 1 --max-steps 20

# full run (L40S, roughly an hour)
uv run modal run cc_finetune.py --run-name ft1 --epochs 12
mkdir -p ../data/results/finetune
uv run modal volume get --env cook --force cc-results /finetune_runs/ft1 ../data/results/finetune/
```

`05_make_holdout.py` prints `holdout 40 (Google clips; 8 from the test split) | val 15 | train 153 originals`. The training log prints the number of training images and confirms that the 40 holdout originals are excluded. Each epoch prints the training loss and the validation IoU and boundary F1 (semantic fusion, threshold 0.4, holes under 25 m² filled); epoch 0 is the untrained head, for reference. The head with the best validation boundary F1 is saved to `cc-sam3-weights:/finetuned/ft1/seg_head_best.pt` and the final epoch to `seg_head_last.pt`; `log.csv` holds the curve. **Check:** validation boundary F1 rises clearly above epoch 0 within a few epochs. If the training loss keeps falling while validation turns down, the best-epoch file has already captured the peak; a second run with `--lr 5e-5` or `--curb-weight 2` is the first thing to try.

**Score on the holdout.** Run the zero-shot baseline and the fine-tuned head on the same 40 holdout clips:

```bash
uv run modal run cc_benchmark.py --run-name ho_zs --subset holdout --modes text --fusions fused \
    --prompt-sets "road,car,crosswalk" --negative-sets "sidewalk,grass,building,tree" \
    --prob-thds 0.15 --fill-holes 25
uv run modal run cc_benchmark.py --run-name ho_ft1 --subset holdout \
    --delta finetuned/ft1/seg_head_best.pt --modes text --fusions semantic,fused \
    --prompt-sets "road" --negative-sets ";sidewalk,grass,building,tree" \
    --prob-thds 0.3,0.4,0.5 --fill-holes 0,25
uv run modal run cc_benchmark.py --run-name ho_ft1_last --subset holdout \
    --delta finetuned/ft1/seg_head_last.pt --modes text --fusions semantic \
    --prompt-sets "road" --prob-thds 0.3,0.4,0.5 --fill-holes 25
for r in ho_zs ho_ft1 ho_ft1_last; do
  uv run modal volume get --env cook --force cc-results /bench_runs/$r ../data/results/bench/
done
```

Each run prints `subset holdout: 40 of 40 listed originals found`. The head is trained on the semantic map for "road", so semantic fusion with "road" alone is the expected winner; the fused and negative-class variants check whether the instance masks or other phrases still help. The zero-shot baseline's settings were chosen on all 165 clips, holdout included, so its holdout score is, if anything, flattering. **Choose:** adopt the fine-tuned head if its best configuration beats the baseline's boundary F1 by more than ~0.05 on the holdout and its QA overlays (`qa/<config>/`) follow the curbs. Record both scores, the run name, and the chosen configuration in `data/results/README`. Score both the best-validation head (`seg_head_best.pt`) and the final-epoch head (`seg_head_last.pt`): with only 15 validation originals, the best-epoch pick is noisy. In run `ft1` the final-epoch head scored higher on the holdout (boundary F1 0.54 vs. 0.49; zero-shot 0.44). Then use `--delta` with the chosen head and configuration in 4.8 and 4.10.

### 4.8 County pilot check

The benchmark is Google imagery only. Check that the top two or three configurations behave on county imagery too, on the pilot set (no labels; visual check):

```bash
uv run modal run cc_fetch.py --source A --input ../data/sample/pilot.csv --subdir pilot_A --out-csv ../logs/pilot_A.csv
uv run modal run cc_fetch.py --source B --input ../data/sample/pilot.csv --subdir pilot_B --out-csv ../logs/pilot_B.csv
uv run modal run cc_segment.py --source A --input-dir pilot_A --pilot --run-name pilot \
    --modes text --fusions semantic --prompt-sets "road" --negative-sets "" \
    --prob-thds 0.3,0.4,0.5 --fill-holes 25 --delta finetuned/ft1/seg_head_last.pt
uv run modal run cc_segment.py --source B --input-dir pilot_B --pilot --run-name pilot \
    --modes text --fusions semantic --prompt-sets "road" --negative-sets "" \
    --prob-thds 0.3,0.4,0.5 --fill-holes 25 --delta finetuned/ft1/seg_head_last.pt
mkdir -p ../data/results/pilot_B
uv run modal volume get --env cook --force cc-results /pilot_B/pilot ../data/results/pilot_B/
```

The values above are the leading holdout configuration from 4.7 (fine-tuned final-epoch head, text prompt "road", semantic fusion, holes under 25 m² filled) at three thresholds. Set `--modes/--fusions/--prompt-sets/--negative-sets/--prob-thds` and `--delta` to the finalists from 4.6 and 4.7 if they differ; text-only modes need no OSM boxes, so step 4.5 can be skipped. Each configuration gets its own folder of QA overlays, and `pilot_summary.csv` reports road fraction, empty-mask rate, and box fall-backs. **Check:** curbs followed on both sources; no systematic failure on county imagery (e.g. leaf-off shadows read as road edges). If county imagery behaves clearly worse for every finalist, label 20–30 county clips the same way as the benchmark before the full run, so B's segmentation quality is measured rather than assumed.

### 4.9 Imagery for the evaluation sample

```bash
uv run modal run cc_fetch.py --source A --input ../data/sample/sample.csv --out-csv ../logs/fetch_A.csv
uv run modal run cc_fetch.py --source B --input ../data/sample/sample.csv --out-csv ../logs/fetch_B.csv
```

**Check:** zero `error` rows; `ground_res_m` ≈ 0.028 for A (zoom 22 at Chicago's latitude) and ≈ 0.049 for B (1024 px over 50 m).

### 4.10 Segmentation

Run the frozen configuration on both candidates (example values shown: the leading holdout configuration from 4.7, final-epoch head; for the zero-shot baseline drop `--delta` and use `--fusion fused --prompts "road,car,crosswalk" --negatives "sidewalk,grass,building,tree" --prob-thd 0.15 --fill-holes-m2 25`):

```bash
uv run modal run cc_segment.py --source A --mode text --fusion semantic --prompts road \
    --prob-thd 0.4 --fill-holes-m2 25 --delta finetuned/ft1/seg_head_last.pt --run-name v1
uv run modal run cc_segment.py --source B --mode text --fusion semantic --prompts road \
    --prob-thd 0.4 --fill-holes-m2 25 --delta finetuned/ft1/seg_head_last.pt --run-name v1
```

Add `--limit 10` for a first plumbing run. **Check:** in `segment_stats.csv`, `empty` is false and `box_fallback_to_text` is rare on nearly all clips; the QA overlays (`mkdir -p ../data/results/qa_B && uv run modal volume get --env cook --force cc-results /B_cook_rgb/v1/qa ../data/results/qa_B/`) follow the curbs.

### 4.11 Grow-cut

Server, minutes; the reference code runs unchanged in its locked environment:

```bash
./03_grow_cut.sh A v1
./03_grow_cut.sh B v1
```

Output per candidate in `data/results/<folder>/v1/`: `refined_crosswalks_v3_0_4.geojson` and `.csv` with `length_ft`. **Check:** similar line counts for A and B; lengths mostly between 20 and 100 ft.

### 4.12 Hand-off to the comparison

Apply the reference study's plausibility filter — drop crossings shorter than 6 ft or longer than 160 ft [@moran2026scaling], which `grow_cut.py` does not apply — when joining A and B to the ground-truth table in R. The QA overlays from 4.10 are a convenient base for the manual measurement pass.

## 5. Notes and Troubleshooting

### Why boxes from OSM

Each box is a 5 m square on an OSM road centre-line, placed on the first ring (15, 11, then 19 m from the clip centre) that crosses a road, so boxes sit on the approach legs rather than in the intersection box. Up to four boxes, at least 6 m apart, fully inside the clip. Typical OSM centre-line offsets of 1–2 m keep a 5 m box on pavement for streets at least ~9 m wide; on narrower streets a box can touch a parkway, which the benchmark and QA overlays will show. Clips with no OSM road nearby fall back to text, flagged in `box_fallback_to_text`.

### Resolution

SAM 3 resizes every input to 1008 × 1008, so keep the 25 m radius fixed across candidates and across the benchmark (whose clips use the same radius). If the fine-tuned head is still not good enough, see the next steps listed under Open Questions in the comparison chapter.

### CRS, datum, and data terms

Cook County serves NAD83(2011) Illinois East (US ft); the fetcher requests EPSG:3857 so both candidates share one grid, and the ≈ 1 m datum shift moves positions slightly but not lengths. Candidate A bulk-downloads Google basemap tiles as the reference study did; Google's Maps Platform terms restrict that, so confirm it fits the project's data-use approvals. The benchmark dataset is CC BY 4.0: credit its authors when reporting results. Running SAM 3 on Modal keeps imagery within the project's own accounts and pins the model version.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `401` / `403` / `GatedRepoError` in `cc_weights.py` | Access not yet approved, or token lacks read scope | Check approval on the model page; recreate the token and the `huggingface` secret |
| `Set ROBOFLOW_API_KEY` | Key not exported in this shell | `export ROBOFLOW_API_KEY=…` (section 3) |
| Benchmark: many images with 0 boxes | File names lack coordinates in that dataset version, or Overpass failed | Check `meta.json`; rerun prep; box-mode configs fall back to text for those images |
| `osm_roads.geojson missing` | A `box` or `text+box` configuration was run without step 4.5 | Run 4.5 including the `modal volume put`, or switch to `--mode text` |
| `ModuleNotFoundError` while building or loading the SAM 3 image | SAM 3 imports a package it doesn't declare (e.g. `pycocotools`) | Add it to `sam3_image` in `cc_segment.py`; the image's build-time import check reports it before any GPU starts |
| Benchmark reports far fewer images than the prep printed | `/bench` on the volume still holds an earlier set | `modal volume rm -r cc-results /bench`, re-upload, and check the `benchmark set:` line printed at the start of the run |
| `[Errno 21] Is a directory` from `modal volume get` | Local destination folder didn't exist | `mkdir -p` the destination first and end it with `/`; the remote folder is written inside it |
| Prep reports 0 `coords-in-name` images | Wrong dataset version (e.g. 6: Esri patches and screenshots only) | `--list-versions`, then rerun prep with a version sized for the reference study's 193 clips |
| Benchmark scores only a handful of images | Dataset version's valid/test splits are tiny | Keep the default `--splits test,valid,train` (augmented duplicates are dropped) |
| `KeyError: 'MODAL_ENVIRONMENT'` | Reference code reads it at import | `export MODAL_ENVIRONMENT=cook` |
| `TypeError: Invalid value '[]' for dtype 'int64'` in grow-cut | Run under pandas 3.x | Run via `03_grow_cut.sh` (reference repo's locked environment) |
| `exportImage failed … 4xx/5xx` | County server busy, or point outside the service extent | Rerun the step (clips are overwritten); lower `max_containers` in `cc_fetch.py` |
| Fragmented road masks | Instance fusion on large "stuff" regions | Use `fused` or `semantic` fusion |
| Road spills onto sidewalks | Sidewalk and road look alike in grey | Add negatives (`sidewalk,grass,building`); compare in the benchmark |
| Grow-cut finds 0 crosswalks | Masks and edges don't overlap | Check both layers in QGIS; edges must come from 4.1 |

: Common failures {.striped}
